collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder who once took advice never to sail to the island on the horizon raises a cup to the life not lived.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: When (name1) was young, an older villager told (him/her) to stay on Isola and never try to sail to the island on the horizon. (name1) listened. (He/she) stayed. (He/she) fished, built, raised children, grew old. Tonight (he/she) looks out at the dark line where that island sits, the same as always. (He/she) has wondered about it a hundred times: was the advice good? Would (he/she) have found something wonderful over there? Or would (he/she) never have come back? (He/she) doesn't know. (He/she) will never know. And tonight, for the first time, (he/she) finds (he/she) doesn't mind not knowing. (He/she) had this life, and it was a good one. Maybe the other one would have been good too. (He/she) raises (his/her) cup to the island on the horizon, and to the person (he/she) might have been over there, and goes to bed.
